name: disk-reader
question: Can the system volume of a stopped server in ${az} (${region}) be read read-only by a Linux reader ECS, its files put into the run's bucket and be attached back to the server as its system volume with the same device name?
about: Reads Windows state (setupapi*.log, System.evtx, Application.evtx, the registry hives SYSTEM and SOFTWARE and the files of the parameter files) of a STOPPED server. The run refuses a server that is not SHUTOFF before it makes anything. It reads the server (system volume, device name, VPC, subnet), makes a bucket named after the project, a security group without an inbound rule and a small Linux reader ECS (no EIP) in the server's subnet and AZ, detaches the system volume of the server, attaches it to the reader and waits for manifest.json in the bucket. The reader (awb/tcp/diskreader.py, the user_data) mounts the volume with ntfs-3g and ro, puts the files under files/ and writes manifest.json last. Then the run detaches the volume from the reader and attaches it back to the server with the same device name. The teardown always gives the volume back first, after a failure too (restore), proves it back with a read and only then deletes the reader and the security group; when the volume is not back the reader stays and the command exits 4. The bucket stays (keep): it holds the files and its expiry tag ends it. The reader uploads with the key of the tenant (the owner's word of 2026-11-25: no IAM agency, no extra keys): the user data is sent as user_data_text with {{secret:obs-ak}} and {{secret:obs-sk}}, which the key service fills with the key of the call; the run never sees the key or the filled script.

server_id.help: the id of the STOPPED server whose system volume is read; the run refuses a server that is not SHUTOFF before it makes anything

az.help: the AZ of the server; the run refuses a server in another AZ

files.help: more files of the volume, a path inside it such as Windows/Panther/setupact.log, up to 20, joined by a colon, a plus for a space; no .., no leading slash

image.help: the name of a public Linux image with python3; ntfs-3g is installed from the image's repository when it is missing

flavor.help: the flavor of the reader; the pattern keeps it small

preflight.says: the server is stopped (SHUTOFF), so its system volume can be detached
preflight.confirm: GET /v1/{project_id}/cloudservers/ID answers server.status SHUTOFF for a stopped server (the read of ecs-boot-ssh)

preflight.says: the server is in the AZ of the run, so the reader can get its volume

steps.says: read the server: its system volume, device name and VPC
steps.confirm: the system volume is the first of server.os-extended-volumes:volumes_attached with bootIndex 0 and carries its device name (/dev/sda) and server.metadata.vpc_id is the VPC; the check sys-first reads the bootIndex

steps.says: read the subnet of the server
steps.confirm: GET /v1/{project_id}/cloudservers/ID/os-interface (OTC ECS API reference, Querying NICs of an ECS) lists interfaceAttachments; net_id is the id of the VPC subnet that a create takes as nics.subnet_id

steps.says: find the public image by its name
steps.confirm: the name and __imagetype=gold filters of GET /v2/cloudimages, as in ecs-boot-ssh

steps.says: the bucket of the run, named after the project; it keeps the files
steps.name: ${name}
steps.keep: holds the files read from the volume
steps.confirm: the create as in obs-policy-deny (PUT /BUCKET through the call operation of the key service); the files are read with awb lab obs get obs://BUCKET/files/... only while a lab run of the project is open and records the bucket (labobs.py), else the owner reads them in the console

steps.says: a security group in the VPC of the server with no inbound rule
steps.name: ${name}
steps.confirm: as in ecs-boot-ssh; a new group holds the default egress rules only, nothing comes in

steps.says: the Linux reader ECS in the subnet and AZ of the server, no EIP
steps.name: ${name}-r

resource.type: ecs reader server with its system disk

steps.confirm: the create body as in ecs-boot-ssh with the user_data_text of awb/tcp/diskreader.py and a random password nobody logs in with (adminPass); whether the platform takes adminPass and user_data together; whether the lab key of the tenant lets the reader put into the bucket of the run; whether the reader reaches the OBS endpoint of the region without an EIP

steps.says: detach the system volume from the stopped server
steps.confirm: DELETE /v1/{project_id}/cloudservers/ID/detachvolume/VOLUME_ID (OTC ECS API reference, Detaching a Disk from an ECS) answers a job; the next step reads the volume. The restore of the teardown is armed before this call

steps.says: attach the volume to the reader
steps.confirm: POST /v1/{project_id}/cloudservers/ID/attachvolume (OTC ECS API reference, Attaching a Disk to an ECS) without a device name: the reader takes the next one

steps.says: the volume is attached to the reader
the reader has put its files and the manifest into the bucket
steps.confirm: a HEAD of an object of a bucket named after the project through the call operation of the key service; 404 until the reader writes manifest.json, last of all
whether the call operation parses a JSON object body into the answer data, so that the check reads result; else the check fails and the manifest is read with awb lab obs get

steps.says: detach the volume from the reader
attach the volume to the server as its system volume with the same device name
steps.confirm: the device name of the system volume, /dev/sda, is the one the attach of a system volume takes

steps.says: the volume is attached to the server
read the volume: which server holds it and under which device name

checks.says: the first volume of the server is its system volume
the server names the device of its system volume
the image is known in the region
the system volume is available after the detach
the volume is in use after the attach to the reader
the reader writes manifest.json into the bucket
the reader mounted the volume read-only and put every file it found
the volume is available after the detach from the reader
the volume is in use after the attach to the server
the server holds its system volume again

restore.says: the system volume of the server is on the server again

actions.says: detach the volume from the reader when the reader holds it
attach the volume to the server as its system volume when nobody holds it

restore.confirm: the volume read GET /v2/{project_id}/volumes/ID answers status and attachments.0.server_id; a detach or an attach is a job, so every action reads until its state holds

reader.confirm: delete_volume true deletes the data disks the reader holds: the restore runs before this delete and a volume that is not proven back keeps the reader alive, so the volume of the server is never attached here

kb.statement: In ${region} the system volume of a stopped ECS can be detached, attached to a Linux ECS in the same subnet and AZ, read read-only there with ntfs-3g and attached back to the server as its system volume with the same device name.
